video_title: Cavs vs Nets | Donovan Mitchell Post Game | 10.24.2026

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on Cleveland's early season turnover issues
quotes.excerpt: some are sloppy turnovers, some are us trying to figure each other out.
quotes.quote: I think the biggest thing is one, some are sloppy turnovers, some are us trying to figure each other out. And when I say that, different connections, whether it's myself and Peyton, or just getting shaking off the rust. Like the one I had to JT, ball just slipped out my hand, right? You got to tighten that up, but that also just comes with being earlier in the season, but something that we have to definitely clean up because that's been the cause of teams coming back.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell says the Cavs need to clean up their early season turnover issues. He admits some are sloppy and some are just the team trying to figure out new connections while shaking off the rust.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell discusses the team's early season turnover issues following a game against the Brooklyn Nets.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on Jarrett Allen's early season impact
quotes.excerpt: he's the X-factor, he's our centerpiece back there, he's doing everything.
quotes.quote: He's the X-factor, he's our centerpiece back there, he's doing everything. He's even knocking down threes confidently, he's getting to the free throw line, he's ducking in, being strong with the ball. That's what you want to see, and it makes our lives a lot easier, selfishly, when he's doing that. So it's great to see that, he's going to continue to be that for us, and him and Evan have been doing a phenomenal job.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell is impressed with Jarrett Allen's start to the season calling him the centerpiece and an X-factor. Mitchell says Allen is knocking down threes and being strong with the ball which makes life easier for everyone else.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell praises the impact of Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley on the team's performance.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on late game execution and closing out games
quotes.excerpt: some of it is late game execution, it's a different five, understanding that.
quotes.quote: To even point, I think turnovers, lapses of who we're closing out to, I think there's just things that just couldn't happen that did happen and we'll go back and assess it. And some of it is late game execution, it's a different five, understanding that, calling different plays, whether it's Peyton in the middle, Peyton getting used to being in that position, myself getting used to where our bigs are ducking in more, right? So getting used to that. Evan did a great job flashing. So we got good looks on the offensive end, I think defensively is really the biggest thing.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell on Cleveland's late game execution. He notes the team is still adjusting to different lineups and roles but emphasizes that defensive lapses are the biggest area that needs to be addressed.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell analyzes the team's late game execution and defensive lapses against the Nets.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the unpredictability of late game defensive pressure
quotes.excerpt: I think there's an unpredictability to it, I think it's just the random.
quotes.quote: I think there's an unpredictability to it, I think it's just the random. I think the NBA is kind of turned into that as a whole. Indiana I think really did a great job of it two years ago and I think everybody kind of followed suit. It was just, just cause chaos and figure out. So usually late game it's like, all right, cool, they're going to do this, boom boom boom, like you think it and when you're picking up full court randomly trapping, there's really no scheme for that.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell says the NBA has shifted toward chaotic defensive schemes. He notes that when teams start randomly trapping full court late in games there is really no scheme for that.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell explains the difficulty of defending against unpredictable late-game defensive pressure.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the value of early season high-pressure games
quotes.excerpt: it builds character of a group, you find out what you're made of.
quotes.quote: It builds character of a group, you find out what you're made of. But also, just like the Brooklyn, it's not Philly, right? Understanding that there's certain things that we were able to get away with because they're young, they're figuring themselves out too. You got a Philly team that's won championships, so it's a little different. But for us, understanding that like it's a mental battle, just continuing to push through that mental. It's not always going to be perfect, but I think for us, having these first two games and different ways, similar but different ways, I think is definitely going to help us in the long run.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell believes early season high pressure games are vital for building character. He says these moments are a mental battle that will help the team in the long run come April May and June.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell reflects on how early season high-pressure games help build team character.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on how the team determines who takes over games
quotes.excerpt: it's a feel thing, tonight Peyton had a mismatch, we went to that action.
quotes.quote: It's a feel thing, tonight Peyton had a mismatch, we went to that action. Tomorrow maybe James, next day maybe me. I think it's more of a feel thing. Obviously myself and James are obviously some of the best scorers to play for sure, but I think it's not just about scoring, it's about getting down and making the right play. I had an isolation, I'm waiting for the double and Flash as I hit him. So I think it's more so that than just like, all right, give the ball and clear out.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell says the Cavs' late game offense is a feel thing rather than just clearing out for stars. He emphasizes that it is not just about scoring but making the right play for whoever has the mismatch.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell explains how the team determines which player takes the lead during offensive possessions.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the team's chemistry and shared winning mentality
quotes.excerpt: when you have a group that wants to win together, I think it's huge.
quotes.quote: When you have a group that wants to win together, I think it's huge. I think understanding that like, okay, I got my guys back, I think that goes a long way. And that goes from spending time together, obviously we built that through the playoffs last year, but spending time together this summer goes a long way. And nights like tonight, nights like the past two nights, continuing to build good habits, continuing to understand that these are working things we can work on, and coming into the gym and working on those different things.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell credits the team's chemistry to time spent together during the summer. He says having a group that wants to win together is huge for building good habits.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell discusses the importance of team chemistry and shared winning mentality.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the importance of the NBA regular season
quotes.excerpt: you can't just show up in April and expect to figure it out.
quotes.quote: You can't just show up in April and expect to figure it out. I think we kind of live in a time where, I mean, and it's for us, like we don't really have much to prove to people so to speak, until we get to April, May, June. But for us internally, we have a lot to prove to ourselves. I don't think it's about the narrative of that. I think this is where you, these two games very well may help us come April, May, June, some to pull from, right? It builds habits. I think the normal NBA fan doesn't understand fully that concept and it's not like nothing bad, it's just like, hey, this is a building block. It's time spent, it's adversity. I think Joe Mazulla said something like everybody loves each other in training camp, right? But you understand like, come December, come January, we're missing shots, we got to get a stop, who are we then?
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell says the Cavs have a lot to prove to themselves internally this season. He emphasizes that you cannot just show up in April and expect to figure it out because these early games are building blocks for later.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell explains why the regular season is essential for building habits for the playoffs.
